audience.text: Python developers building document-processing workflows, automation tools, or LLM-agent integrations that require PS/EPS/XPS conversion, rendering, or metadata extraction.

capabilities.text: Parse PostScript and Encapsulated PostScript files using a full interpreter and extract DSC/EPS metadata.
capabilities.title: Read and parse PS/EPS documents

capabilities.text: Load XPS packages and navigate fixed pages and print tickets through XpsDocument APIs.
capabilities.title: Read and parse XPS documents

capabilities.text: Create new documents from scratch using PsDocument.create() or XpsDocument.create() and draw content via PsCanvas or XpsDocumentBuilder.
capabilities.title: Author PS/EPS and XPS documents

capabilities.text: Write PS/EPS and XPS content to PDF 1.4 using PdfWriter with font embedding support.
capabilities.title: Convert to PDF output

capabilities.text: Render PS/EPS and XPS content to PNG, JPEG, BMP, or TIFF using RasterRenderer with Skia or fallback Python renderer.
capabilities.title: Rasterize to image formats

capabilities.text: Expose conversions and metadata extraction as MCP tools (ps_to_pdf, xps_to_pdf, eps_metadata, etc.) for automation.
capabilities.title: MCP tool exposure

capabilities.text: Construct page content with RenderModelBuilder, supporting paths, text, images, and clipping operations.
capabilities.title: Programmatic page building

capabilities.text: Embed TrueType/Type1 fonts in PDF output using FontResolver and FontCache with explicit font folder paths.
capabilities.title: Font embedding for PDF

limitations.text: No PDF import or parsing API is provided; the library only writes PDF, it does not read existing PDF files.
XPS-to-image conversion always requires the Skia backend (skia-python) and has no pure-Python fallback.
Importing aspose.page.pdf.writer or aspose.page.image.raster_renderer before aspose.page.ps raises a circular-import error in a fresh interpreter.
Font embedding requires explicit font paths via FontResolver; automatic system-font discovery is not provided.
The MCP server only exposes conversion and metadata tools; document creation APIs (PsDocument.create, XpsDocument.create) are not available as MCP tools.
The library targets Python 3.10+ and does not support earlier versions.

problems_solved.text: Enables conversion of PS/EPS and XPS documents to PDF and raster formats (PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF) using a pure-Python implementation backed by skia-python for rendering.
Supports programmatic page creation and editing through RenderModelBuilder, allowing users to build documents from scratch without existing input files.
Exposes document conversions as MCP tools for LLM-agent and automation workflows via FastMCP-compatible HTTP endpoints.
Extracts EPS metadata such as bounding box and title without full document rendering.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Page FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for reading, authoring, and converting PostScript, EPS, and XPS documents to PDF or raster formats without external dependencies like Ghostscript.

workflows.name: PS to PDF conversion
workflows.text: Use the ps_to_pdf handler to convert a PostScript file to PDF by specifying input and output paths.

workflows.name: XPS to PDF conversion
workflows.text: Call xps_to_pdf with an input XPS file path and desired output PDF path to generate a PDF document.

workflows.name: Programmatic PDF creation
workflows.text: Build a RenderDocument using RenderModelBuilder, add text and paths, then write it to PDF using PdfWriter.

workflows.name: Raster rendering to PNG
workflows.text: Render a RenderDocument to a PNG image using RasterRenderer and encode it with encode_png.

workflows.name: EPS metadata extraction
workflows.text: Extract EPS metadata including bounding box and title using the eps_metadata handler.

workflows.name: MCP server deployment
workflows.text: Start an MCP server exposing conversion tools (ps_to_pdf, xps_to_pdf, etc.) for remote automation.
